children: Arabica coffee futures on the ICE exchange hit a fresh 10-week low on Wednesday given benign weather in Brazil and surging exports, while raw sugar hit a two-week trough.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled down 2.1 cents, or 0.7%, at $2.8155 per lb, having hit a 10-week low of $2.7705 earlier.
* "ICE stock levels remain low, but the market is being pressured by reports of strong exports out of Brazil and good growing weather for the 2027 crop," said broker ADMIS.
* Top grower Brazil's green coffee exports in the first two weeks of September stood at a daily average of some 13,500 metric tons, up 51.5%, data showed.
* Exchange arabica stocks (KC-TOT-TOT), however, increased to 233,479 bags later on Wednesday as ICE released their daily report, moving away from a 27-year low of 217,646 bags, data showed.
* ICE said 16,210 bags passed quality checks to enter the certified stocks, while 2,960 failed.
* Robusta coffee
fell 1.5% to $3,430 a metric ton.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
was little changed at 17.97 cents per lb, having hit its lowest since September 3 earlier at 17.68.
* Oil prices slipped, tempting cane mills in Brazil and India to produce more sugar and less ethanol, a cane-based biofuel.
* Sugar has lost some ground after its recent run-up to a 16-month high, but remains underpinned by potential production declines in India, the European Union and Thailand, dealers said.
* The weather in Brazil will mostly dry up in the next 10 days, allowing sugar cane harvest to continue.
* France is set for its smallest sugar beet harvest since the 1970s after heat waves and drought shrivelled crops in the EU's biggest agricultural producer, the farm ministry said.
* White sugar
​settled down $2.30, or 0.4%, at $524.00 a ton.
COCOA
* London cocoa
​settled up 63 pounds, or 1.5%, to 4,377 pounds per ton.

* Cocoa buyers in No. 2 grower Ghana are owed about 4 billion cedi ($349 million) by regulator COCOBOD for last season's crop and want it paid before the new crop year begins, an industry body told Reuters.
* Ivory Coast's cocoa grind, a measure of demand, rose 21.3% year-on-year in August to 47,646 metric tons of beans, industry data from the world's top cocoa grower showed.
* New York cocoa
rose 0.9% to $5,979 a ton.
